cards.prompt: Define Parameter-sensitive plan. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The plan whose best access path changes across parameter values distributions prepared-statement modes or cached decisions.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The directed operator tree whose leaves access data and whose internal nodes transform row streams with estimated properties.
major_error_concepts: Reading only the top cost and missing the subtree that creates excess rows.
cards.prompt: Define Physical plan tree. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The directed operator tree whose leaves access data and whose internal nodes transform row streams with estimated properties.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The engine algorithm implementing a scan join sort aggregate or materialization with required inputs produced properties and resource behavior.
major_error_concepts: Naming an operator without its preconditions or row behavior.
cards.prompt: Define Physical query operator. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The engine algorithm implementing a scan join sort aggregate or materialization with required inputs produced properties and resource behavior.

cards.definition:
**Definition.** Plan inspection reads either a nonexecuting estimated operator tree or an execute-capable plan with observed rows and timing, with the mode, parameters, settings, and side effects declared. Estimated plans do not prove execution behavior; execute-capable inspection can run mutations and must use an appropriate rollback or safe fixture.

**Worked check.** An estimated plan predicts 10 rows for an index scan; execute-capable inspection observes 8,000 rows and a spill. Only the latter supplies runtime evidence. Running that mode on `DELETE` can perform the delete, so use a disposable fixture or a verified rollback boundary.
major_error_concepts: Calling EXPLAIN proof the query ran or using execute-capable inspection on a mutation casually.
cards.prompt: Distinguish estimated from execute-capable plan inspection and state the mutation-safety boundary before inspecting a data-changing statement.
required_concepts: Estimated plan inspection reads a nonexecuting estimated operator tree.
Execute-capable plan inspection runs the statement and reports observed rows and timing.
Plan evidence declares whether the inspection mode was estimated or execute-capable.
Plan evidence records the parameters used for inspection.
Plan evidence records the relevant database settings.
Plan evidence records any side effects produced by inspection.
An estimated plan does not prove execution behavior.
Execute-capable inspection of a data-changing statement can perform the mutation.
A data-changing statement may be inspected in execute-capable mode only within an appropriate rollback boundary or a safe disposable fixture.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The sampled or maintained summaries such as row count distinctness null fraction frequency histogram and dependency data used for estimates.
major_error_concepts: Running ANALYZE as ritual without checking data freshness sample or estimate repair.
cards.prompt: Define Planner statistics. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The sampled or maintained summaries such as row count distinctness null fraction frequency histogram and dependency data used for estimates.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The movement or evaluation of filters as early as semantics permit to reduce rows while respecting outer joins volatility and null behavior.
major_error_concepts: Moving predicates for speed and silently converting outer join semantics.
cards.prompt: Define Predicate placement. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The movement or evaluation of filters as early as semantics permit to reduce rows while respecting outer joins volatility and null behavior.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The early removal of unused columns to reduce row width while retaining all attributes needed by later predicates joins ordering and output.
major_error_concepts: Removing an attribute still needed downstream or confusing SQL projection with set duplicate elimination.
cards.prompt: Define Projection placement. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The early removal of unused columns to reduce row width while retaining all attributes needed by later predicates joins ordering and output.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The selection among sequential index bitmap or other documented scans based on predicates selectivity ordering visibility and cost estimates.
major_error_concepts: Forcing an index scan because an index exists or declaring sequential scan wrong.
cards.prompt: Define Scan-operator choice. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The selection among sequential index bitmap or other documented scans based on predicates selectivity ordering visibility and cost estimates.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The ordering operation with keys directions null rules memory run generation merge spill and top-N variants qualified by engine.
major_error_concepts: Treating sort cost as row count only or omitting a deterministic tie key.
cards.prompt: Define Sort operator. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The ordering operation with keys directions null rules memory run generation merge spill and top-N variants qualified by engine.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The mode in which each statement is ordinarily its own transaction unless an explicit transaction groups statements under product and driver rules.
major_error_concepts: Assuming consecutive statements on one connection commit together.
cards.prompt: Define Autocommit boundary. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The mode in which each statement is ordinarily its own transaction unless an explicit transaction groups statements under product and driver rules.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The interleaving of transaction read write commit and abort operations preserving each transaction's program order.
major_error_concepts: Summarizing transactions as simultaneous and omitting the decisive operation order.
cards.prompt: Define Concurrent schedule. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The interleaving of transaction read write commit and abort operations preserving each transaction's program order.

cards.definition: **Definition.** A schedule whose precedence graph is acyclic and can be transformed by swapping nonconflicting operations to a serial order.
major_error_concepts: Calling every schedule with correct final values serializable or treating conflict serializability as all possible equivalence notions.
cards.prompt: Define Conflict-serializable schedule. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: A schedule whose precedence graph is acyclic and can be transformed by swapping nonconflicting operations to a serial order.

cards.definition: **Definition.** Conflicting database operations are operations from different transactions on the same logical item where at least one writes and reversing their order can change behavior.
major_error_concepts: Calling operations conflicting because they run concurrently or touch one table broadly.
cards.prompt: Define Conflicting database operations. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: Conflicting database operations belong to different transactions.
Conflicting database operations access the same logical item.
At least one of the two conflicting operations is a write.
Reversing the order of conflicting operations can change the schedule's behavior.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The all-or-none effect of a declared transaction on database state after commit abort or crash under engine assumptions.
major_error_concepts: Extending database atomicity automatically to a provider API call or emitted email.
cards.prompt: Define Database atomicity. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The all-or-none effect of a declared transaction on database state after commit abort or crash under engine assumptions.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The named position allowing partial rollback inside an open transaction without independently committing preceding work.
major_error_concepts: Calling release savepoint a durable commit or assuming external effects roll back.
cards.prompt: Define Database savepoint. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The named position allowing partial rollback inside an open transaction without independently committing preceding work.

cards.definition: **Definition.** A transaction reading another transaction's uncommitted write that may later abort.
major_error_concepts: Calling any changed value a dirty read after the writer already committed.
cards.prompt: Define Dirty-read anomaly. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: A transaction reading another transaction's uncommitted write that may later abort.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The documented set of snapshots anomalies conflicts and abort behavior for a named level in one product and operation mix.
major_error_concepts: Using the level name alone as a portable complete concurrency specification.
cards.prompt: Define Isolation-level contract. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The documented set of snapshots anomalies conflicts and abort behavior for a named level in one product and operation mix.

cards.definition: **Definition.** A lost-update anomaly occurs when two transactions derive writes from an overlapping prior value and one committed update overwrites the other without preserving both intents.
major_error_concepts: Assuming both commits imply both increments were retained.
cards.prompt: Define Lost-update anomaly. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: A lost-update anomaly begins when two transactions derive writes from an overlapping prior value.
One committed update then overwrites the other transaction's update.
The overwrite fails to preserve both transactions' intended effects.

cards.definition: **Definition.** A transaction rereading one item and seeing a committed change by another transaction between reads under its snapshot contract.
major_error_concepts: Calling a changed query result a phantom without identifying the same logical item.
cards.prompt: Define Nonrepeatable-read anomaly. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: A transaction rereading one item and seeing a committed change by another transaction between reads under its snapshot contract.

cards.definition: **Definition.** A repeated predicate query returning a changed qualifying row set because another transaction inserts deletes or changes predicate membership.
major_error_concepts: Calling any nonrepeatable value a phantom or assuming row locks protect a predicate range universally.
cards.prompt: Define Phantom-read anomaly. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: A repeated predicate query returning a changed qualifying row set because another transaction inserts deletes or changes predicate membership.

cards.definition: **Definition.** A schedule executing each complete transaction without interleaving and serving as a reference outcome not necessarily the only correct execution.
major_error_concepts: Calling a schedule serial because commits are ordered while operations interleave.
cards.prompt: Define Serial transaction schedule. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: A schedule executing each complete transaction without interleaving and serving as a reference outcome not necessarily the only correct execution.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The database rejection of a transaction whose concurrent execution cannot safely commit under the selected serializable mechanism and evidence.
major_error_concepts: Treating serialization failure as random infrastructure noise or retrying only the last statement.
cards.prompt: Define Serialization failure. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The database rejection of a transaction whose concurrent execution cannot safely commit under the selected serializable mechanism and evidence.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The preservation of declared database constraints and application invariants when each transaction is correct rather than a magic ACID service.
major_error_concepts: Saying ACID consistency means data is semantically correct regardless of transaction code.
cards.prompt: Define Transaction consistency qualification. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The preservation of declared database constraints and application invariants when each transaction is correct rather than a magic ACID service.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The survival of committed database effects across specified failures under storage configuration acknowledgment and recovery assumptions.
major_error_concepts: Treating a returned statement row before commit or non-durable setting as durable completion.
cards.prompt: Define Transaction durability. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The survival of committed database effects across specified failures under storage configuration acknowledgment and recovery assumptions.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The restriction on effects and observations among concurrent transactions whose exact guarantee depends on level engine operations and retry behavior.
major_error_concepts: Interpreting isolation as no concurrency or no need to analyze anomalies.
cards.prompt: Define Transaction isolation. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The restriction on effects and observations among concurrent transactions whose exact guarantee depends on level engine operations and retry behavior.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The directed graph with one node per transaction and an edge for each ordered conflicting-operation pair used to test conflict serializability.
major_error_concepts: Drawing edges from commit order or nonconflicting reads.
cards.prompt: Define Transaction precedence graph. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The directed graph with one node per transaction and an edge for each ordered conflicting-operation pair used to test conflict serializability.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The replay of all database decisions after a retryable concurrency failure using fresh reads bounded attempts idempotency and separated external effects.
major_error_concepts: Retrying a suffix with stale values or duplicating a provider call from the aborted attempt.
cards.prompt: Define Whole-transaction retry boundary. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The replay of all database decisions after a retryable concurrency failure using fresh reads bounded attempts idempotency and separated external effects.

cards.definition: **Definition.** A write-skew anomaly occurs when transactions read overlapping constraints and then write disjoint items so each local check passes while the joint invariant fails.
major_error_concepts: Looking only for same-row write conflicts and declaring snapshot execution safe.
cards.prompt: Define Write-skew anomaly. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: A write-skew anomaly begins when transactions read overlapping constraints.
The transactions then write disjoint logical items.
Each transaction's local constraint check passes.
The combination of the committed writes violates the joint invariant.

cards.definition:
**Definition.** Commit retry and reconciliation uses transaction identifiers, idempotency or deduplication, authoritative readback, and application-specific recovery to resolve an uncertain outcome before applying another effect.

**Worked check.** After COMMIT for payment key p17 times out, perform authoritative, sufficiently consistent readback for p17. If it confirms the effect, reconcile; if it proves absence after transaction resolution, retry with the same key. If absence cannot be established, keep the outcome unknown rather than issuing an unkeyed second charge.
major_error_concepts: Retrying until success without checking whether the original effect already committed.
cards.prompt: A client times out after submitting COMMIT for payment idempotency key p17, so the server may already have committed. What authoritative readback and branching decision must occur before another charge attempt?
required_concepts: Commit retry and reconciliation identifies the intended effect with a transaction identifier or an idempotency or deduplication key.
After the commit response is lost, the client performs an authoritative and sufficiently consistent readback for that identifier before applying another effect.
If readback confirms the original effect, the client reconciles and does not issue another charge.
If readback proves absence after transaction resolution, the client may retry using the same idempotency key.
If absence cannot be established, the client keeps the outcome unknown and uses application-specific recovery rather than issuing an unkeyed second charge.

cards.definition: **Definition.** A database commit point is the irreversible or durably recoverable protocol state after which recovery must preserve the transaction's effects under the declared failure model; it is independent of whether the client receives the commit response.
major_error_concepts: Equating SQL COMMIT invocation or returned rows with the durable commit point before acknowledgment.
cards.prompt: Define Database commit point. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: A database commit point is the protocol state at which the transaction is irreversible or durably recoverable.
After the commit point, recovery must preserve the transaction's effects.
The preservation claim is limited to the declared failure model.
Whether the client receives the commit response does not determine whether the database crossed the commit point.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The cycle of transactional waits that cannot resolve without abort release or external action with victim and retry effects preserved.
major_error_concepts: Calling every timeout a deadlock or retrying without rolling back failed transaction state.
cards.prompt: Define Database deadlock. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The cycle of transactional waits that cannot resolve without abort release or external action with victim and retry effects preserved.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The required sequence for log journal metadata and data persistence whose violation can expose unrecoverable partial state.
major_error_concepts: Assuming storage writes reach durable media in issue order without barriers or guarantees.
cards.prompt: Define Database flush ordering. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The required sequence for log journal metadata and data persistence whose violation can expose unrecoverable partial state.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The protected database object level such as row key range page table or schema whose scope affects contention overhead and anomaly coverage.
major_error_concepts: Assuming row locks protect absent rows or a multirow invariant automatically.
cards.prompt: Define Database lock granularity. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The protected database object level such as row key range page table or schema whose scope affects contention overhead and anomaly coverage.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The table specifying which requested and held lock modes may coexist on the same object under a product contract.
major_error_concepts: Deciding compatibility from transaction purpose rather than declared modes.
cards.prompt: Define Lock compatibility matrix. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The table specifying which requested and held lock modes may coexist on the same object under a product contract.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The upgrade or downgrade of a held lock whose wait and deadlock effects depend on concurrent holders.
major_error_concepts: Assuming an upgrade is immediate because the requester already holds a weaker lock.
cards.prompt: Define Lock conversion. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The upgrade or downgrade of a held lock whose wait and deadlock effects depend on concurrent holders.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The retention of obsolete versions or cleanup delay caused by old active snapshots with storage and performance consequences.
major_error_concepts: Blaming vacuum or storage growth without locating the retained visibility horizon.
cards.prompt: Define Long-snapshot reclamation pressure. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The retention of obsolete versions or cleanup delay caused by old active snapshots with storage and performance consequences.

cards.definition: **Definition.** A stored logical-row version with creation deletion or transaction visibility metadata allowing snapshot reads under an engine contract.
major_error_concepts: Calling versions independent rows or assuming old versions persist forever.
cards.prompt: Define MVCC row version. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: A stored logical-row version with creation deletion or transaction visibility metadata allowing snapshot reads under an engine contract.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The engine-qualified predicate deciding whether a row version is visible from snapshot transaction identifiers commit state and the reader's own actions.
major_error_concepts: Reading the version with largest identifier as automatically visible.
cards.prompt: Define MVCC visibility rule. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The engine-qualified predicate deciding whether a row version is visible from snapshot transaction identifiers commit state and the reader's own actions.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The concurrent attempt to change overlapping logical state whose resolution can block abort overwrite or serialize despite nonblocking reads.
major_error_concepts: Saying MVCC means writers never block or conflict.
cards.prompt: Define MVCC write conflict. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The concurrent attempt to change overlapping logical state whose resolution can block abort overwrite or serialize despite nonblocking reads.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The recorded recovery boundary summarizing or constraining work needed after crash without necessarily forcing every transaction state to final storage immediately.
major_error_concepts: Treating a checkpoint as a full backup or proof no earlier page needs analysis.
cards.prompt: Define Recovery checkpoint. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: A recovery checkpoint is a recorded recovery boundary.
The checkpoint summarizes or constrains the work required after a crash.
Recording a checkpoint does not necessarily force every transaction state to final storage immediately.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The conceptual read-compatible and write-exclusive protection modes on a governed object with exact product modes qualified.
major_error_concepts: Calling every SELECT lock-free or treating conceptual S and X as exact vendor mode names.
cards.prompt: Define Shared-and-exclusive lock intent. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The conceptual read-compatible and write-exclusive protection modes on a governed object with exact product modes qualified.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The visibility reference defining which committed versions and own writes a transaction or statement can observe under its isolation level.
major_error_concepts: Treating snapshot time as wall-clock exactness or assuming all levels use one transaction snapshot.
cards.prompt: Define Transaction snapshot. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The visibility reference defining which committed versions and own writes a transaction or statement can observe under its isolation level.

cards.definition: Two-phase locking separates a growing phase, when a transaction may acquire locks but releases none, from a shrinking phase, when it releases locks but acquires no new ones. With the required operations and conflicts covered by the lock protocol, this yields conflict serializability. Strict 2PL retains exclusive/write locks until commit or abort, preventing other transactions from observing uncommitted writes through conflicting accesses. It is unrelated to two-phase commit.
major_error_concepts: Calling acquire A, release A, acquire B a two-phase-locking trace.
Confusing the lock-acquisition protocol with distributed two-phase commit.
cards.prompt: Define Two-phase-locking structure. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: After the first lock release, no new locks may be acquired in basic 2PL.
Strict 2PL retains write locks through commit or abort; the locking coverage is what supports conflict serializability.

cards.definition:
**Definition.** An uncertain commit outcome occurs when a client loses the response around the commit boundary and cannot infer from the transport failure alone whether the transaction committed, aborted, or remains unresolved under recovery.

**Worked check.** After `COMMIT`, the connection drops before acknowledgment. The client marks the outcome unknown rather than rolled back, then checks a transaction or business key in a new session before deciding whether compensation or retry is safe.
major_error_concepts: Treating a timeout as proof of abort and blindly repeating a non-idempotent transaction.
cards.prompt: What boundary or limitation does uncertain commit outcome impose?
required_concepts: An uncertain commit outcome arises when the client loses the response around the commit boundary.
The transport failure alone cannot distinguish whether the transaction committed, aborted, or remains unresolved under recovery.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The idempotent reconstruction that removes effects of incomplete transactions and reapplies durable committed effects according to logged history.
major_error_concepts: Redoing every record blindly or undoing a committed transaction because its page was not flushed.
cards.prompt: Define Undo-and-redo recovery. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The idempotent reconstruction that removes effects of incomplete transactions and reapplies durable committed effects according to logged history.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The distinction among memory cache kernel buffers device caches and persistence domains under the storage and power-failure assumptions.
major_error_concepts: Treating process memory or an fsync request as universal persistence proof.
cards.prompt: Define Volatile-and-durable database state. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The distinction among memory cache kernel buffers device caches and persistence domains under the storage and power-failure assumptions.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The directed graph from waiting transactions to transactions holding incompatible locks used for deadlock diagnosis.
major_error_concepts: Drawing resource nodes as transactions or inferring a cycle from long wait time alone.
cards.prompt: Define Wait-for graph. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The directed graph from waiting transactions to transactions holding incompatible locks used for deadlock diagnosis.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The durable change record or original-state journal written under an ordering protocol so committed work can be redone or incomplete work undone.
major_error_concepts: Calling an application audit table the recovery log or writing data before recoverable intent.
cards.prompt: Define Write-ahead log or rollback journal. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The durable change record or original-state journal written under an ordering protocol so committed work can be redone or incomplete work undone.
